title: model2data metrics 0.1.0
description: The metrics of a model2data model: a `<stem>.metrics.yml` file beside `<stem>.model2data.yml`. Normative together with README.md in this directory, which says what a document means and the checks a reader makes beyond this schema (against the model, among others).

model2data-metrics.description: The version of the metrics spec the document is written against. A reader refuses a minor version it does not implement (the spec is before 1.0.0).

model.description: The `name` of the model the metrics are for. A metrics file read against a model of another name is an error.

metrics.description: The metrics, by name. Order is significant: consumers list them in document order.

dimensions.description: Which columns are offered as dimensions, beyond the default (every enum, boolean, date and timestamp column that is not a key), by column path. `false`: never offered. `true` or a mapping: offered, with its label and description.

infer.description: Whether every `measure` column of the model also yields a metric (default true). false: only the metrics written here.

metricName.description: A metric name: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and underscores.

columnPath.description: A column of the model: `table.column`, or `schema.table.column`. The last `.` separates the column.

tableKey.description: A table of the model: its name, or `schema.name`.

metric.description: One metric. Exactly one of `measure` (simple), `count` (a row count), `ratio` and `expression` (derived) says its kind.

description.description: What the metric is, in prose.

ai_context.description: Prose for an AI tool: when to use the metric, what it is called, what it is not.

format.description: How a value is shown. It changes no value: `percent` expects a fraction (0.6 is shown as 60%), and a consumer passes it on as a percent format without multiplying.

measure.description: A simple metric: this column, aggregated by `agg`, or without it by the column's own `measure` in the model (`true` is sum).

agg.description: How a simple metric aggregates its column. `count` and `count_distinct` apply to any column; the rest to numeric ones.

count.description: A row count: the rows of this table (that pass `where`).

ratio.description: The numerator metric's total divided by the denominator metric's: a ratio of totals, null when the denominator is zero or null.

expression.description: A derived metric: arithmetic over metric names and numbers, with + - * / and parentheses (the grammar is in README.md). Division by zero is null.

time.description: The date or timestamp column a simple metric or row count is dated by: on its table, or reachable through many-to-one references. Default: the table's first date or timestamp column, else the first one reachable.

where.description: A filter on a simple metric or a row count: every entry must hold. A key containing a `.` is a column path and maps to its condition; `any` holds when one of its filters does, `all` when every one does. A column must be on the metric's table or reachable through many-to-one references along exactly one path.

value.description: A value a column is compared with: an enum member, true or false for a boolean column, a number for a numeric one, an ISO 8601 date or timestamp string for a date or timestamp one, text for any other.

condition.description: What a column must hold. A value: equal to it. A list: one of them. A mapping of operators: every one must hold. A null fails every condition but `is_null: true`, as in SQL.
